name: Spirit Elk-Maddened Creature (CR +1)
body:
A Spirit Elk-Maddened creatures are always solitary beings, many of them even before the transformation. While they look physically similar to their former selves, the madness enhances their strength and gives them a modicum of the Spirit Elk’s powers, simultaneously driving them to constantly seek out challenging opponents until one of them eventually claims their life.

Creating a Spirit Elk-Maddened Creature

“Spirit Elk-Maddened” is an acquired template that can be added to any animal or humanoid (referred to hereafter as the base creature).

A Spirit Elk-Maddened creature uses all the base creature’s statistics and special abilities except as noted here.

Challenge Rating: Same as base creature +1.
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil.
Senses: A Spirit Elk-Maddened creature gains darkvision +60 ft. and low-light vision.
Defensive Abilities: A Spirit Elk-Maddened creature gains cold resistance 10, immunity to fatigue, DR 5/cold iron and fast healing 10
Abilities: Str +4, Dex +2, Con +4, Int -4 (minimum 1), Wis -2, Cha -2

One story associated with the Spirit Elk is particularly interesting, and it is of the hero Ragnar the Raving. A mountain of a man, a great warrior of strong arm, but very susceptible to emotion. When his village came under the Spirit Elk’s reign of terror, Ragnar set out by himself and, armed with his cold iron spear, slew the beast in combat, barely surviving and losing one of his ears and a few digits to frostbite. When he returned home and recuperated, Ragnar became increasingly tormented by the idea that the Spirit Elk is not really dead and will come back for him and his loved ones. After a few months, the paranoia got to him so much that he decided to go into a self-appointed exile, which very shortly turned into a quest to find the beast before it finds him. And so, after a long search, find the beast he did. Ragnar slew the beast again, and a few times after that, each time destroying more of the body and taking more bloodied bones as trophies to assure himself that the monster is dead. Inevitably, a great warrior he was, age and wear on the body has caught up to Ragnar. He wasn’t killed the Elk, whom some people have started to jokingly call his only friend. He met his end when, looking for the beast, he wandered into the territory of an ancient white dragon that made that particular stretch of emptiness his home. The memory of Ragnar is not the only thing left after his passing, for the bones he collected from each successful slaying of the Spirit Elk were taken by a cabal of shamans assembled by a powerful, monstrous warlord, himself believed to be a vessel of a Spirit Elk, and forged with magic, steel and blood into a set of armor. The warlord died after a prolonged campaign, but the armor reportedly refused destruction and resurfaces in the world from time to time.
